newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Maintenance March-June profit below target.
newsitem.headline: Japan Maintenance March-June profit below target.

text.p: Building facility maintenance firm Japan Maintenance Co Ltd said on Wednesday its parent current profit in the four months to June 30 was 13.8 percent smaller than its target.
Japan Maintenance president Osamu Shikata told Reuters that the company's sales in the first four months of this business year ending February 28, 1998, were also 0.6 percent below the target.
"We have not been able to achieve targetted profit and sales so far in the first half of this business year," Shikata said.
But he said the company maintained its parent earnings forecast for the current business year as it expects to receive large contracts to manage buildings in the second half of the business year.
In April, the company announced that it expected its parent current profit for 1997/98 to grow to 2.15 billion yen from 1.71 billion yen from a year ago.
It also said that parent sales in 1997/98 were expected to be 43 billion yen against 1996/97 parent sales of 40.06 billion yen.
The smaller-than-expected profit and sales during the first four months of the fiscal year were partly due to a decline in the number of contracts to manage buildings, Shikata said.
It also reflected the fact that parking lot projects were smaller in size than originally expected, he said.
Japan Maintenance builds parking lots and offers building maintenance and cleaning services.
He said that the company would try to improve management to cut costs, which have climbed due to an increase in personnel costs, Shikata said.
